entries.name: DROPBOX_APP_KEY
entries.description: The app key of the store's KaratOS app in the Dropbox App Console, a scoped app with only files.metadata.read and files.content.read turned on.
howToGet: Signed in to Dropbox as the account that holds the folder, open the App Console and create an app with Scoped access and Full Dropbox access, named KaratOS.
In the app's Permissions tab, tick only files.metadata.read and files.content.read (account_info.read is always on), and save.
Copy the App key from the Settings tab.

entries.name: DROPBOX_APP_SECRET
entries.description: The app secret of the KaratOS app, which goes with each token refresh. It also checks the signature on Dropbox webhooks.
howToGet: In the KaratOS app's Settings tab in the App Console, choose Show next to App secret.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: DROPBOX_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the account owner approving the KaratOS app once with offline access. Each sync uses it for a four-hour token asked for read scopes only, and stops if Dropbox reports any other scope.
howToGet: Signed in as the account owner, open https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<app key>&response_type=code&token_access_type=offline&scope=files.metadata.read%20files.content.read and choose Allow. Dropbox shows a code.

Exchange the code once with a POST to https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, the code, and the app key and secret, run on the host. The answer's refresh_token is the value.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: DROPBOX_FOLDER
entries.description: The folder to read, with everything below it, as the Dropbox website shows its path. In a team space that path starts at the team's root, such as /Accounting/Statements.
howToGet: Open the folder on the Dropbox website and copy its path from the breadcrumb, starting with /. Choose a folder that holds only the store's documents, not the whole Dropbox.

entries.name: DROPBOX_FILE_NAMES
entries.description: keep (the default) keeps file and folder names, which can name customers; drop keeps only ids, kinds and times.
howToGet: Leave unset to keep names. Set drop if the store names files after customers and would rather not keep them.
